incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: prod-inference-p95-spike detected for service=redwood-runtime v3.2.1. Multiple pages sent to #eng-oncall. Auto-escalation to oncall: Sam Patel.

Sam Patel: taking the bridge. quick summary: p95 token latency jumped from ~220ms -> ~1.8s starting ~15m ago for inference requests routed to pool:eu-west-2-gpu-a. Some customers observed timeouts. I'm primary for next 2h. Priya, can you be secondary?

Priya Singh: on it, switching to secondary now. ping me if I should jump to the bridge.

Alex Chen: adding some metrics — p95 by model shows spike concentrated on model=llama-70b-q4 at seq_len>1024. throughput looks steady though.

Miguel Torres: noticed increased eviction rates on node gpu-10-az1. Kernel OOM logs show repeated memory pressure. I pulled node logs, see repeated GC/pager churn.

Jenna Li: customer impact: three high-usage tenants reported timeouts and elevated latency (support tickets #3451, #3452, #3453). No data exfiltration. Inform SRE and support.

Sam Patel: mitigation checklist from runbook: 1) confirm affected pool & model 2) toggle fallback to smaller model variant 3) drain suspected node 4) scale-up GPU pool if capacity available. I'm trying fallback now.

Sam Patel: executing model fallback to llama-70b-q4 -> llama-13b-q4 for routes with seq_len>1024. Command:```api v1 route update --route inference/stream --model-override "llama-13b-q4" --condition "seq_len>1024"```

incident-bot: ACTION: fallback applied to 12 routes. Observe traffic shifting.

Priya Singh: running the PromQL query for p95 by node:```sum by(node) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, node)))``` saw node gpu-10-az1 at 1.9s, others ~300ms.

Miguel Torres: starting drain on gpu-10-az1. kubectl cordon gpu-10-az1 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-10-az1 -n prod-inference. Watch for eviction failures.

Alex Chen: note: KV-cache hit rate dropped ~12% in same window — maybe cache eviction due to memory pressure. If we restore node count, cache warming might take ~10-20min.

Jenna Li: I'm drafting customer comms to affected tenants — include ETA 30-45m and mitigation steps. Support will post updates to tickets.

Sam Patel: current status: fallback in place, p95 dropped to ~650ms cluster-wide but still ~1.1s on one AZ. We're draining the bad node. No more new pages as of now.

Priya Singh: still watching evictions; autoscaler did not trigger because commit-level reserved capacity hit. Suggest manual scale-up if drain doesn't relieve pressure in 10m.

Miguel Torres: manual scale-up attempted: increased pool eu-west-2-gpu-a by 2 nodes via infra console (request id infra-req-8842). If provisioning stalls, we should failover traffic to another region.

Sam Patel: runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference/p95-spike. Key sections: "model_fallback", "node_drain_and_recover", "region_reroute". Also see the quick commands block.

Sam Patel: quick diagnostic snippets pasted for handoff:```# check p95 by route
curl -s "http://metrics.internal/api/query?query=p95_inference_by_route" | jq .

# check node memory
kubectl top node gpu-10-az1

# list pods evicted
kubectl get pods -n prod-inference --field-selector status.phase=Failed | grep OOM```

Priya Singh: taking over primary in 30m while Sam steps out for sync. I'll keep bridge open and update every 15m or on change. Noted gap: overnight 02:00-06:00 UTC coverage is light — Sam, can you add a follow-up note for the next rotation?

Sam Patel: will add a shift note. Next steps I'm leaving for Priya: 1) confirm post-scale p95 stabilizes 2) if not, shift traffic to eu-central-1 fallback pool 3) coordinate with infra for node healthchecks and possible AMI rebuild.

incident-bot: PAGE: Priya Singh (secondary) has been paged as backup.

Jenna Li: support note: customers notified, CS handling refunds/escalations as needed. Tracking impact window 21:10-21:45 UTC.

Miguel Torres: post-drain telemetry: p95 on gpu-10-az1 traffic drained, p95 cluster now ~420-700ms depending on model. Eviction counters trending down. Need to schedule postmortem runbook tasks: root-cause (node kernel oom vs model memory regression).

Priya Singh: accepted handoff. Primary now. I will run a brief sanity sweep in 10m: checks: a) route fallback correctness b) pool capacity c) node reboots. If stable for 30m, we'll close bridge and create follow-up postmortem ticket.

Sam Patel: added a quick handoff note to rotation doc: "Observed capacity saturation due to large-seqlen workload on llama-70b-q4; applied targeted fallback; manually scaled pool; drained bad node. Priya primary for next 2h."

Jenna Li: suggest we add a short-term policy to fallback earlier on p95>800ms for big models, to avoid customer-facing timeouts. I'll file a product request.

Alex Chen: action item for infra: add an alert for cache-hit-drop >10% coincident with p95 spike. Miguel can you add?

Miguel Torres: will file infra alert PR.

Priya Singh: last update before brief: p95 stabilized to ~480ms overall, affected tenants still in support but no new errors. Bridge remains open until 22:00 UTC for observation. I'll escalate earlier if needed.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (provisional): latency back within target for most routes. Follow-up: postmortem and RCA assigned to Miguel Torres and Alex Chen.

Sam Patel: thanks team. I'll follow up with a short blameless postmortem and make sure handoff notes get into the daily oncall summary.

Jenna Li: closing comms on support side, will update tickets once postmortem link is up.

Priya Singh: handoff complete — leaving detailed notes in the handoff doc and will create the follow-up ticket: PROD-8765.

Sam Patel: handed off. good job all. :thumbsup:
